newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish O/N up on new reserve period, zloty weakens.
newsitem.headline: Polish O/N up on new reserve period, zloty weakens.

text.p: The Polish overnight deposits rates opened nine points higher from Friday's lows on Monday's 166 million zloty net outflow from the system, and the market was balanced in early trade, dealers said.
They said banks prefered to build up average accounts on new September reserve period starting on Monday than to lend surpluses at lower rates on the market.
"Market's new equilibrium level, slightly below the main central 14-day drainage level of 19.05 percent reflected the begining of a new reserve period," said Andrzej Hirsz from Bank Gdanski SA.

At the 0745 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 18.75/19.10 percent, up from 18.0/19.0 percent at the opening and 7.0/11.0 percent on Friday. Tomorrow/next rates were quoted at 18.75/19.10 percent, up from Friday's 18.2/18.8 percent.
Dealers said that the central bank was likely to refrain from offering NBP-bills on Monday, because it did not want to compete with the treasury's primary T-bill auctions.

Some analysts expected T-bill yields to inch up at Monday's 700 million zloty tender as the recent yield slide resulted from surplus cash spilling over from the money market rather than fundemental factors, such as falling inflation.
On the secondary market the benchmark 52-week T-bill yield rose 0.05 point to 19.40/19.30 percent against the average yield of 19.46 percent sold at last Monday's primary tender.

The zloty drifted down to 1.72/1.66 percent from the trading band centre in light trade against opening's 1.80/1.69 percent on the back of small speculative currency purchases, but it was seen remaining boxed in between 1.8 and 1.6 percent.
At 0830 GMT it was quoted at 2.7440/60 to the dollar, down from opening's 2.7420/50 and at 1.8510/20, down from 1.8495/15.
